⭐ ARC Raiders – Honest, No-BS Review

ARC Raiders is one of those games that looks incredible on the surface—flashy sci-fi world, smooth movement, great atmosphere—and it actually delivers some fun moments, especially in PvE. But it’s also a game that constantly shoots itself in the foot with design choices that frustrate players more than they excite them.

Let’s break it down.

🎮 PvE – The Part That Actually Works

PvE is hands-down the strongest part of ARC Raiders.

What’s Good

Combat feels satisfying: The movement, gunplay, and physics all blend well when you’re fighting AI. There’s a weight to the weapons and a cinematic feel to engagements.

Robots and encounter design: Some of the robots are genuinely fun to fight—tough but fair, with patterns you can learn and counter.

Exploration and atmosphere: The world is gorgeous and has that ruined-future aesthetic that makes simple wandering enjoyable.

What Holds It Back

Repetition: After a while, missions start to feel the same. Hop in, loot some area, fight the same bots, extract. Rinse, repeat.

AI can swing between dumb and unfair: Sometimes bots stand still waiting to be deleted. Sometimes they instantly lock on and melt you.

Still, PvE is where the game shines. If ARC Raiders leaned fully into PvE, it might have been great.

⚔️ PvP – Fun on Paper, Toxic in Reality

The moment ARC Raiders shifts into PvP territory, things get messier.

Why It’s Fun (Sometimes)

Chaotic, adrenaline-pumping encounters when squads collide in the middle of a bot fight.

Smart plays feel rewarding: In theory, outmaneuvering or outsmarting another squad feels amazing.

Why It’s Toxic (Often)

Third-partying is constant: You can win a full fight and then instantly lose to a squad that only showed up at the end. It feels cheap.

Balance issues: Some weapons and gear make PvP wildly uneven, turning fights into who-shot-first contests.

Sweaty players farm casuals: Exactly what ruins extraction shooters—pros hunting new players = a rough onboarding experience.

Communication is rough: Teaming, backstabbing, and general PvP saltiness create a more toxic environment than fun.

PvP feels like it was added because extraction shooters need PvP—not because the game was designed to support it well.

💰 Loot – The Weakest Part of the Game

Loot in ARC Raiders is… disappointing. Let’s call it what it is.

The Problems

Not enough variety: A lot of the gear feels samey, and upgrades don’t feel impactful enough.

Low drop quality: You often grind for 20 minutes only to walk away with something you don’t care about.

Risk vs reward is off: You risk a full loadout in PvP just to maybe get a green item that you’ll scrap anyway.

Progression feels slow and unrewarding: The game doesn’t give enough fun loopholes or power spikes to keep you hooked.

In an extraction shooter, loot is the motivation—and here, it often feels like busywork.

⚙️ Technical & Quality of Life

Optimization is decent, but still has dips in high-intensity areas.

Audio design is great, adding tension and style.

User interface can feel clunky, especially when checking inventory or crafting.

Nothing game-breaking, but definitely not perfect.

⭐ Overall Verdict

ARC Raiders has a strong PvE foundation wrapped in a beautiful world, but PvP toxicity and weak loot progression hold it back from greatness.

It’s fun when things click—but inconsistent enough that those moments don’t happen as often as they should.

If you like:

✔ Atmospheric sci-fi worlds
✔ PvE combat
✔ Extraction-style tension
…you’ll enjoy parts of it.

If you hate:

✘ PvP third-partying
✘ Toxic lobbies
✘ Weak loot systems
…this game will frustrate you—often.

This game is worth every penny. A friend of mine and I jumped in hoping not to get disappointed and I can assure you Embark Studios didn't.

THE COMBAT
It may feel a bit stiff at first, but it's grounded and feels realistic, it's not jumping up and down and flying from left to right and hitting trickshots. It's tactical game play, whether it's ARC(AI) or Raiders(Real players). The ARCs may feel a bit OP at first, but you just have to learn how to handle each one of them and then you'll be just fine.

ATMOSPHERE/MAP
The atmosphere of ARC Raiders is just perfect. The perfect apocalyptic feel. Somehow it feels empty yet so full. Even though the maps are small, you'll never be bored.

RACE AGAINST TIME
Like in every extraction shooter it's a race against time. You have to fight your way through everything to get what  you need and leave in time. ARC Raiders is no different. You spawn, you see a timer in your screen which can be different every game. Sometimes you have 30 minutes, sometimes maybe only 15 minutes. There are extraction points all across the map but each of them closes after a period of time. You are able to extract with multiple teams at a time if you're willing to make peace with each other.

GAMEPLAY
The mix of surviving, looting and shooting makes this feel like you're in a real apocalypse. Always on the edge with your ears wide open and when you finally are able to extract with good loot --> satisfaction. The proximity chat makes the game so much more fun, being able to communicate with your fellow raiders: making peace or fighting until death. It's all in your hands.

TEAM/SOLO
It doesn't matter if you're playing in team or solo, you'll always be having fun and will always be on edge. I must be honest though, while playing solo there is a greater chance people will team with you. While being in a team often scares people. Though to some people it may seem unfair being able to go 1 vs 3 or 2 vs 3, I personally think it makes this game even more exciting. Really having to think about your next move and trying to outsmart the others. Whether it are the ARCs or the Raiders.

SPERANZA
In a way it's sad that you can't walk in Speranza and that it's just your menu but I kinda get it. It would be a big game otherwise and a bit heavy for your console or pc.

DEVELOPMENT
You can really feel that the developers of Embark Studio really put their effort in this one. The graphics are awesome, the gameplay is smooth with minor bugs. Which I will admit there are some but they are so small that they don't get in the way of your awesome gameplay.

PERFORMANCE
I got no complaints, got no difficulty only while loading the map but that is normal. No FPS drops, no lagging. Nothing at all, love it.

COSMETICS AND CUSTOMISATION
There isn't much customisation yet, at least not if you're not willing to pay extra. The cosmetics are expensive, 20 euros for a skin but I mean, in which game isn't it this expensive nowadays. They have some really cool cosmetics if you're willing to pay the price, and each cosmetics has its own customisation options. That makes it way more fun, so you can choose if you want to wear a hat or the glasses and so on.

CONCLUSION
If you really like a mix of PvP, PvE and an extraction shooter than this is the game for you. It's a great balance between surviving, tense combat and looting. It doesn't feel repetitive at all but that is my personal opinion. I am writing this review the day I bought this game and already got almost 8 hours in it. The game runs smoothly with no FPS drops and no crashes.

Overall, ARC Raiders is pure awesomesauce. 
It has a few rough edges but they still got time to fix those, it got just released after all. This game is totally worth it.

[h1]Summary[/h1]

[b]Extremely high production quality with poor gameplay design between players.[/b]


[h1]PVP hot take[/h1]

[b]PVP makes this a miserable experience. It doesn't even make sense for the last survivors of humanity to murder each other while killer robots attempt to exterminate them all.[/b]

[i]Fighting players is not balanced - if you get hit first while out of cover, you're dead. Every step of progress is threatened with the possibility of wasting your time. If you don't have 4-8 hours a day to grind materials, find blueprints, and get the best gear, then you'll never be able to compete with the sweats who do.[/i]


[h1]Why sweaty people love this[/h1]
[b]I can see the appeal of an experience like this, but it's only really for people who love a good old fashioned power imbalance. [/b]

[i]The lulgitgud bros enjoy having power over others; they take great joy in exerting power over people with less, new players, and folks looking for cooperative play. Do they desire digital domination because they wield no true power IRL and desperately crave any form of control so they can feel like the true navigators of their own lives? Who's to say, I'm not a sweat psychologist, but it kinda tracks eh?[/i]


[h1]Why friendly people love this[/h1]
[b]The world building, art direction, and tonal vibe of the universe is absolutely incredible.[/b] 

[i]Scavenging for materials while outwitting homicidal machines is fun as hell. Foraging for your chickenbro is wholesome and adorable. Seeing another player in trouble and helping them out is satisfying af. Ganging up on quadruped tankbots with a bunch of random raiders is truly exhilarating. Listening to the terrifying world around you live and breathe is invigorating. All of these aspects of the game are top notch, and they deserve a thoughtful game design to be appreciated in full.[/i]


[h1]The bottom line... and money[/h1]
[b]We all know this was a PVE experience that pivoted hard into a PVP extraction shooter. We can all see the bones of a magnificent PVE game trapped in the skin of a PVP sweatfest. And that's the most disappointing aspect of this entire thing.[/b]

[i]As it currently exists, Arc Raiders at best suffers from an identity problem, and at worst is another form of exploitative capitalism. Allow me to explain: It's reasonable to assume these decisions were made so the studio could enjoy a more lucrative outcome for their product. If progress can be made moot at any moment, and progress is the only way to accrue power and improve your odds of survival, then consumers are likely to spend plenty of time chasing that power in-game. The more time consumers spend in-game, the more likely they are to make additional purchases of skins and currency. At about 20 dollars a pop for skins, that's a good probabilistic model for additional revenue on top of the base cost of the game itself. This isn't far off from how a publisher like EA designs layered systems to squeeze every probable dollar out of their own customers.[/i]

[b]The design is a form of manipulation disguised as a competitive game, and I'm not for it.[/b]


[h1]Thoughts and prayers, I hope you get better soon[/h1]
[b]I'm putting this down until something changes, and if nothing changes, that's fine.[/b]

[i]It was a fun 30 hour Arc Raiders binge week. I had my fun and I'd like to continue, but with so many other options out there for similar if not more satisfying gameplay loops, I'll pass for now.[/i]
